source.citation: Lothenbach, B., Winnefeld, F., Alder, C., Wieland, E., Lunk, P. (2007). Effect of temperature on the pore solution, microstructure and hydration products of Portland cement pastes. Cement and Concrete Research 37(4), 483-491.
source.location: Section 2 and Table 1 (p. 484), Sections 3.2 and 4.1 (pp. 486-489), Table 2 (p. 487), Fig. 8 (p. 490)

transcription.from: the published article (PDF): Table 1 footnotes, Table 2 and the text read in the text layer and checked on the rendered pages; Fig. 8, a raster image (754 x 661 pixels), digitized at its native resolution
transcription.note: The cements are the SRPC (CEM I 52.5 N) and PLC (CEM II/A-LL 42.5 R) of Lothenbach et al. (2008), whose Table 1 (in Lothenbach2008.json: chemical_analysis, normative_phases) repeats this paper's Table 1; it is not transcribed again here. What this file adds is what Lothenbach2008.json does not hold: the sulfate carriers and the readily soluble alkalis of the Table 1 footnotes, the PLC alkali rows where the two papers differ, the measured TGA contents and phase observations, Table 2, and the pore solutions of Fig. 8 at 28 and 150 days. The early-age points of Fig. 8 (1 h to 1 day) and Figs. 1 to 4 (alite XRD peak heights, TGA curves, strengths) are not transcribed: they describe hydration kinetics, not the equilibrium against temperature.

water_cement_ratio_srpc_paste.description: Water/cement ratio of the SRPC pastes (1 kg of cement per batch, cast in sealed 0.5 l PE bottles) whose solids and pore solutions were analyzed at 5, 20 and 50 C.

water_cement_ratio_plc_paste.description: Water/cement ratio of the PLC pastes analyzed by TGA and XRD after 28 days at 5, 20, 30 and 40 C (the PLC mortars and concretes were at 0.58).

preconditioning_time.description: Water, cement and aggregates were stored this long at the curing temperature before mixing.

al_so3_molar_ratio_plc.description: Molar Al/SO3 ratio of the PLC (mol/mol), printed '2.8 mol/mol'.

al_so3_molar_ratio_srpc.description: Molar Al/SO3 ratio of the SRPC (mol/mol), printed '1.9 mol/mol'.

monosulfate_observed_temperature_srpc.description: Curing temperature, degrees Celsius, at which monosulfate (XRD, TGA/DTG, EDX of platelets) was found in the 150-day SRPC paste, formed at the expense of ettringite and monocarbonate; it was not found at 5 and 20 C. No temperature between 20 and 50 C was tested on the SRPC.

digitization.tool: each marker located on the native-resolution image (754 x 661 pixels) from the vertical extent of its dark and grey pixels, its center taken at the middle of that extent; mapped through the decade tick marks of each panel (pixel rows 10/100/189/279 for 1 to 0.001 mol/l in the OH-/Ca panel, 10/77.5/144/212/279 for 1 to 0.0001 in the Na/sulfate panel, 347/436.5/525/615 for the K (1 to 0.001) and Si (0.01 to 0.00001) axes, 345/399/453 and 54 pixels per decade for the Al/Fe panel from 1E-4 to 1E-9)
digitization.note: A fully visible marker is read to +-1.5 pixel, a marker partly hidden by another (its center inferred from one vertex and the marker height, 12-14 pixels) to +-3 pixels; the uncertainty column converts that into concentration (4 to 14 %). The x positions of the late markers (pixel 253 and 292 in the first panel) map to 28 and 147 days. Markers wholly hidden by another of the same series are not given a value: hidden_markers lists them; the paper states that after 150 days the concentrations are similar at 5, 20 and 50 C except sulfate, Al and Fe.

notes: Table 1 of this paper and Table 1 of Lothenbach et al. (2008) give the same SRPC column. For the PLC they differ in the alkali rows of the normative composition: 2007 prints K2SO4 1.4, Na2SO4 0.29, K2O 0.08 and Na2O 0.15 g/100 g where 2008 prints 1.1, 0.23, 0.25 and 0.18 (plc_alkali_normative_rows holds the 2007 values). The 2007 Table 1 also lists 'CaO 1.7 / 0.45' in the normative composition, the free lime of the chemical analysis.

The calculated hydrate assemblage against temperature (SRPC and PLC at 150 days, 0 to 60 C) is in Lothenbach et al. (2008), Figs. 5 and 6, already transcribed in Lothenbach2008.json (hydrate_volumes, transition_temperature 48 C, range 42-54 C); this paper has no calculation.

Section 3.3: the higher sulfate at 50 C is attributed to the increase of ettringite solubility with temperature and to the precipitation of monosulfate instead of ettringite; the paper adds that the sulfate concentration and pH of the pore solution, and not only the temperature, decide between ettringite and monosulfate.
The SRPC pastes were not cooled back after curing at 50 C: there is no measurement of a reversal (ettringite re-forming), which is the delayed-ettringite step proper.
